raw.assessment: The incumbent achieved 32/40 intended course sets and a 17-minute median, missing both targets. Its seven-minute median for unchanged assignments supports retaining the basic CSV workflow, but does not establish causation. Six affected exports coincide with assignment changes; applying current assignments to a requested historical week is a plausible failure mechanism. The two renamed-course cases limit that account: omitted records and name-based checking confusion remain distinguishable explanations. Replacement delay greatly exceeds execution time, without identifying its cause. Zero observed cross-center rows offers bounded reassurance; the unsampled course split remains an explicit coverage gap.

openings.claim: Current-assignment selection may change a past week’s exported course set when an instructor is reassigned.
openings.delta: Separate requested-week membership from mutable current assignment before choosing an implementation.
openings.prediction: Holding attendance and the intended weekly course set fixed, changing only current assignment changes exported membership; requested-week selection removes that sensitivity.
openings.probe: In fabricated staging, export an identical past week before and after reassignment. Trace inclusion decisions, then compare against a manually specified intended set. Bound investigation and any prototype within six engineer-days, retain the documented CSV, and verify concurrent attendance entry without adding hosting resources.
assumptions: Historical membership has an agreed meaning across centers.
A deployable correction depends on sufficient assignment history or another authoritative weekly membership source; neither is established.

openings.claim: Do renamed courses actually lose attendance rows, or do coordinators reject complete files because schedule and export names differ?
openings.delta: Test the supplied counterexample with row-level completeness and observed checking behavior.
openings.prediction: Complete participant/session coverage with failed name matching supports recognition confusion; missing expected rows supports an export-selection defect. Both can coexist.
openings.probe: Use the six consenting coordinators’ two short sessions with fabricated renamed-course fixtures and their usual schedule formats. Independently compare expected rows and time checking, downloading, correction, and import. Include a split-course fixture as coverage exploration. Keep artifacts private and CSV unchanged; share the same six-day budget.
assumptions: Fabricated tasks approximate ordinary checking sufficiently to discriminate mechanisms; they cannot establish next-40-export success.

raw.assessment: The sample meets neither the course-set target nor the handling-time target. Assignment changes and renames are associated with affected exports, but their causal role is unestablished. Zero observed cross-center rows does not cover the unsampled split-course case. The following capability and benefit remain hypotheses.

openings.claim: A private, week-aware course resolver could produce the documented CSV alongside a center-local checklist identifying the courses represented for that week, despite assignment changes or renames.
openings.delta: Full capability depends on stable course identities, effective-dated assignments and names, explicit split-course semantics, center authorization checks, and reads that permit concurrent attendance entry. Presently testable fragment: a staging resolver over fabricated transition histories and coordinator-agreed expected course sets; historical reconstruction in production is not assumed available.
openings.prediction: If current-state interpretation causes the affected selections, holding attendance fixed while changing assignment or name will change incumbent course membership but leave week-aware membership aligned with the agreed expectation.
openings.probe: Cap implementation and testing at six engineer-days on existing staging resources. Compare incumbent and prototype outputs for fabricated reassignment, rename, split, and cross-center identity-collision cases. Check exact expected course membership, authorized rows, documented CSV compatibility, and successful concurrent attendance entry. Stop at the prototype if production dependencies exceed the budget.
assumptions: Fabricated histories can encode coordinator-agreed week and split semantics.
A staging-only fragment fits existing hosting; production feasibility remains unverified.

openings.claim: Would an explicit expected-course checklist reduce coordinator handling, or does spreadsheet import account for most of the excess time?
openings.delta: Separates a course-verification benefit from an unobserved spreadsheet bottleneck using timed actions.
openings.prediction: If uncertainty about course coverage drives handling, the checklist will shorten checking time with little change in import time; an import bottleneck predicts little total benefit.
openings.probe: Use the six coordinators' two sessions for counterbalanced, matched fabricated exports with and without a checklist. Time checking, correction, download, and import separately, and record course-set errors. Treat results as preliminary; assess the stated targets on the next 40 exports only after any deployment.
assumptions: Fabricated tasks approximate ordinary spreadsheet work.
Sessions and checklist preparation share the six-day budget.

openings.claim: Current assignments may distort historical membership; a private week-aware resolver could correct it.
openings.discriminator: Fixed attendance, varied assignment/name: compare incumbent/prototype with agreed weekly sets.
openings.probe: Fabricate reassignment, rename, split and cross-center identity collisions; verify membership, authorization, CSV and concurrent entry.
openings.uncertainty: Stable identities, effective-dated assignments/names, weekly/split semantics and authoritative history remain unestablished; stop at prototype if dependencies exceed budget.

openings.claim: Rename failures may involve missing rows, recognition confusion, or both.
openings.discriminator: Check participant/session completeness independently of name matching.
openings.probe: Observe fabricated rename/split checks with usual schedule formats alongside D3.
openings.uncertainty: Timetable completeness/timing and task realism unknown.

openings.claim: A center-local weekly course checklist may reduce checking; import may dominate instead.
openings.discriminator: Checking improves versus little total benefit with unchanged import burden.
openings.probe: Six coordinators, two sessions: counterbalance matched fabricated exports with/without checklist; time checking, correction, download, import; record errors.
openings.uncertainty: Preliminary sessions cannot establish operational success.

lineage.reason: Resolver with Z1; checklist with A2.

post_distill.decision: Probe before deployment. Shared limits: six engineer-days, existing hosting, private authorized workspaces, documented CSV, uninterrupted attendance entry. Split-center isolation remains uncovered; replacement-delay cause unknown. After justified deployment, assess next 40 exports: median <=12 minutes, intended sets >=95%, zero foreign-center records. Evidence is synthetic.
